comment: What a race is: the port, the rounds, the droplets and the workloads. RACING.md says how a race uses them.

workloads.name: plaintext
workloads.title: Plaintext
workloads.summary: GET /plaintext answers 13 bytes over kept-alive connections: the cost of HTTP itself.

workloads.name: echo-4k
workloads.title: Echo 4 KiB
workloads.summary: POST /echo with a 4 KiB body, answered with the same bytes: reading bodies and writing larger responses.

workloads.name: templates
workloads.title: Templates
workloads.summary: GET /menu renders a 12-row HTML table from a template per request, every value escaped: the work of a server-rendered page.

workloads.name: sse
workloads.title: SSE (Datastar)
workloads.summary: GET /sse with Datastar's signals in the query, answered with a stream of ten Datastar events, a chunk each: the work of a Datastar action.

workloads.name: churn
workloads.title: Connection churn
workloads.summary: GET /plaintext on a new connection every request: accepting, and closing, as fast as possible.

workloads.name: plaintext-h2
workloads.title: Plaintext, HTTP/2 (h2c)
workloads.summary: GET /plaintext over HTTP/2 without TLS: 32 connections of 8 streams each, the same 256 requests in flight as Plaintext's 256 connections: the cost of HTTP/2's frames, HPACK and multiplexing, without TLS (browsers always add it).

workloads.name: plaintext-tls
workloads.title: Plaintext, HTTP/2 + TLS
workloads.summary: Plaintext, HTTP/2's shape, over TLS: against Plaintext, HTTP/2 (h2c), the cost of TLS a request.

workloads.name: echo-4k-tls
workloads.title: Echo 4 KiB, HTTP/2 + TLS
workloads.summary: Echo 4 KiB over HTTP/2 and TLS, 128 connections of 2 streams: bodies both ways, encrypted.

workloads.name: templates-tls
workloads.title: Templates, HTTP/2 + TLS
workloads.summary: GET /menu over HTTP/2 and TLS, 128 connections of 2 streams: a server-rendered page as browsers fetch it, with no proxy in front.

workloads.name: sse-tls
workloads.title: SSE (Datastar), HTTP/2 + TLS
workloads.summary: The Datastar action over HTTP/2 and TLS, 128 connections of 2 streams: as browsers send it, with no proxy in front.

workloads.name: churn-tls
workloads.title: Connection churn, HTTP/1.1 + TLS
workloads.summary: A new TLS connection every request, a full handshake each (no resumption), HTTP/1.1: what a new visitor costs.

workloads.name: conduit
workloads.title: RealWorld (Conduit)
workloads.summary: An article listing, an article, a comment and a favorite, all at once, on SQLite (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL).

workloads.name: conduit-tls
workloads.title: RealWorld (Conduit), HTTP/2 + TLS
workloads.summary: RealWorld's mix over HTTP/2 and TLS, 128 connections of 2 streams: an application as browsers reach it, with no proxy in front.

open_loop.comment: The ladder each workload marked "ladder" climbs after the rounds. None is marked since 2026-10-10: RealWorld's climb is the open loop (owner).
